subject: Re: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities for Global Labs — TIA scoping
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@globallabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@globallabs.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities — initial ask

Hi Vivek / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We need a concise mapping for Global Labs so our privacy/legal teams can complete the TIA and decide whether the UK Addendum (IDTA) is required for our UK processing. Key asks:

- Short narrative of where customer data is processed (region-by-region) and which Redwood subprocessors touch PII.
- Confirmation of the legal mechanism you expect us to use (SCCs + TIA, or UK IDTA + TIA).
- A stub list of evidence we can expect (SOC2 report link, encryption-at-rest docs, subprocessor access controls).
- A target timeline — procurement needs to close by end of March if possible.

I've attached a spreadsheet with our initial TIA questions (global-labs-tia-questions.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the TIA template verbatim or whether legal wants modifications?

Appreciate a short call if it helps.

Thanks,
Sarah Bennett
Head of Privacy Operations
Global Labs

Attachment: global-labs-tia-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@globallabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities — initial ask

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Answers at a high level below; Kimberly and Marissa have added more technical and contractual color in-line.

Summary (short):
- Processing locations: primary inference & KV cache on our eu-west-1 region (Ireland). For burst/dedicated capacity we may route to eu-central-1 and us-west-2 depending on customer settings.
- Subprocessors: infra providers (GCP/Google Cloud EU), S3-equivalent object store for artifacts (provider varies by deployment), telemetry/metrics vendor for operational logs, and our CDNs for model artifacts distribution.
- Legal mechanism: SCCs + TIA is our standard for customers with EU data. For UK-based processing we offer the UK Addendum (IDTA) as an alternative. We can sign the IDTA if Global Labs prefers — the content differs primarily in the transfer safeguard clauses and annex mapping.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (link below), encryption at rest + in transit summary (attached), subprocessor access matrix (we will provide).

We can take the TIA template, and our legal team will review any changes quickly — small redlines are fine but renegotiating core transfer clauses will add time.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to drop the processing map (short diagram).
2) Marissa to attach draft UK Addendum if you want that route.
3) Quick 30-min sync tomorrow to confirm nucleus of the TIA.

Attachments: processing_map_v2.png (diagram, 48 KB)

--
Vivek Kulkarni

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-14T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities — technical / subprocessor note

Hi all — adding a bit more technical specificity to accelerate your privacy review. Short bullets so you can drop into the TIA: 

- Data classes: request metadata (timestamps, user-id hash), prompt text (customer-provided; flagged as PII if present), model-generated outputs (may contain customer data), and operational logs (traces, error logs).
- Data residency: For Global Labs' tenant we will default to eu-west-1 for both inference and KV caching. Dedicated/deployment-specific fallbacks to other regions are explicitly opt-in on the contract and documented in the annex.
- Subprocessors (short list):
  - Google Cloud (GCP) — compute + object storage (EU regions).
  - FastEdge CDN — artifact distribution (global).
  - LogSight (metrics vendor) — aggregated telemetry, no raw prompt storage unless enabled by customer.

- Access controls: role-based access (RBAC), IAM with short-lived credentials for infra engineers, and strict MFA enforcement for SREs. Audit logs are retained 90 days in standard plan; extended retention is an add-on.
- Technical mitigations for transfers: AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, optional client-side encryption for sensitive artifacts.

TIA scoping advice:
- If Global Labs wants to rely solely on SCCs, we need to confirm the Subprocessor Annex and flow-down obligations.
- For UK IDTA: draft is standard and requires a small processing map + subprocessor list; it will substitute the SCC annex.

I'll attach a quick processing map and a stub subprocessor matrix (see processing_map_v2.png). Happy to jump on a technical call.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: processing_map_v2.png (diagram, 48 KB)

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@globallabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities — clarifying items

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we accept either SCCs+TIA or IDTA+TIA: 

1) For prompts that include customer PII, do you persist full prompt text by default? We need to know retention policy and whether prompt redaction/pseudonymization is an option.
2) For subprocessor notifications, what lead time do you provide when onboarding a new subprocessor that has access to PII?
3) SOC2: can you provide the latest Type II report (or a read-only link) and a brief summary of any exceptions in the last 12 months?

Procurement note: if we sign the UK Addendum, legal can close faster on our side but compliance will still want the SOC2 and the processing map.

If you can share the SOC2 link and a one-pager on retention/psuedo options, procurement and privacy will move quickly. Can we aim to close this week?

Regards,
Sarah

P.S. We're happy to take the IDTA if Redwood thinks that's a simpler path — just confirm the differences we should expect in the annexes.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@globallabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer scope & processor responsibilities — next steps & evidence links

Sarah — short answers and next steps: 

1) Prompt persistence: by default we retain prompt text for 30 days in the hosted plan for debugging and safety. We offer a pseudonymization feature (hashing and sensitive-field redaction) and a client-side encryption option for longer-term artifacts. I'll include a one-pager on retention and pseudonymization in the shared Drive link.
2) Subprocessor notification: standard notice is 30 days for non-critical additions; for subprocessors that will access PII we provide 10 business days and an escalation path if you require immediate review. Critical security-related subprocessors (e.g., new identity providers) are coordinated directly with your security team.
3) SOC2: link below is a read-only console for the latest Type II report (we'll provide a signed copy under NDA). There were two low-severity exceptions last quarter (config drift on a non-production logging bucket) — both remediated and documented in the SOC2 annex.

Evidence links / attachments:
- SOC2 read-only: https://redwood.security-console/soc2/type2/2026 (access requires the token we'll share)
- One-pager: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-example (contains retention & pseudonymization options)
- Attached: processing_map_v2.png, uk-addendum-draft-Redwood.docx

Proposed commitment: Redwood will produce the subprocessor matrix and SOC2 summary by tomorrow EOD and finalize the IDTA if you want that route. If you want to sign SCCs+TIA instead, we'll add the subprocessor flow-down language to the SCC annex and provide the same evidence pack.

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow morning CET to finalize which mechanism you prefer?

Best,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
